en: Theragāthā 6.2 Chakkanipāta,
Paṭhamavagga (The First Chapter)
The Verses of the Elder Tekicchakāri:
“The rice is harvested,
the paddy has gone to the threshing floor.”
"I do not obtain alms;
how shall I sustain myself?
"Recall the Buddha, who is immeasurable, with a mind full of faith."
Your body will be suffused with rapture; you will be constantly uplifted.
Recollect the immeasurable Dhamma with confidence;
your body will be suffused with rapture; you will be constantly uplifted.
“Recall the Sangha, which is immeasurable, with a mind full of faith;
your body will be suffused with rapture and you will be constantly uplifted.
“You dwell in the open air.”
"These nights are wintry; do not be distressed by the cold.
Enter the monastery, its doors bolted shut."
“I shall touch the four immeasurables,
and through them I shall dwell in happiness;
I shall not be distressed by cold.”
“Dwelling unshaken,” said the Elder Tekicchakārī.
… [The Elder Tekicchakārī] … [continued].
